text:
sara: FYI, we just got an urgent escalation from ACME Corp — they say audit logs for several API keys are missing between 2026-03-10 00:00 UTC and 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC. Security is asking for scope + customer notification plan. Can ops/devs triage?

alex_support: copying the ticket here — customer reports 5 keys, return code 200 for requests but the corresponding audit entries don't appear in their exported logs. No billing issues reported on their side.

mike_sre: quick check: ingestion pipeline had a brief backlog on 2026-03-10 ~03:40 UTC due to a controller restart during a rolling host update. Backlog cleared by 04:10 but need to confirm whether entries were dropped or just delayed.

lina_security: important: if entries were dropped for the time range, this is a data retention integrity issue. We need: 1) definitive scope (which customers/keys), 2) root cause, 3) whether HSM/KMS operations overlapped, 4) timeline for customer-facing note.

jordan_product: ACME is SOC2 concerned, they already flagged this to their compliance lead. We should prepare a short timeline and a single-point contact. Suggested: acknowledge within 24h, full update within 72h.

alex_support: repro steps I ran (local):
```
# hitting their keys with a curl loop
for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate; done
# then checking audit export JSON: they have no entries for 2026-03-10 02:xx
```

mike_sre: dug into the raw queue metrics: at 03:37-03:45 utc we saw ~15% increase in dropped messages on the ingestion shard that handles our audit export pipeline. The shard recovered when the controller rebalanced. No errors from storage layer (S3) afterwards.

lina_security: did any KMS/HSM rotation happen in that maintenance window? If a rekey or HSM failover happened, logs may have been temporarily unseal-rejected.

opsbot: scheduled_kms_rotation: completed 2026-03-10 03:30 UTC on cluster-eu-2; rotation status: success; some clients saw transient decrypt errors 03:30-03:36 UTC.

mike_sre: ok that matches. There were transient decrypt errors reported by the ingestion worker at 03:32 which caused retries; the controller restart overlapped with the KMS rotation ~03:30-03:40 which led to a small window where messages timed out and weren't requeued correctly. We're still validating whether those messages hit dead-letter queue.

alex_support: ACME says they exported a full audit archive (their end) and cannot find entries. They want to know if logs can be reconstructed or if they'll need a statement that entries are unavailable.

lina_security: we need to classify impact: if messages are in dead-letter queue or S3 temporary buffer, we can reconstruct; if dropped pre-enqueue, we must treat as irrecoverable. Prioritize reconstruction.

mike_sre: immediate actions: 1) check DLQ for ingestion-shard-7 for 03:20-04:00 UTC (in progress), 2) search raw kafka topic partitions for missing offsets (in progress), 3) snapshot controller logs and KMS audit for correlation (in progress). ETA for initial findings: 3 hours.

jordan_product: good. Communications: draft ack to ACME: short note confirming we received escalation, we are investigating and expect initial findings in ~3 hours, escalation to security & SRE happening now. Keep it factual, avoid speculative language about dropped logs.

alex_support: I'll send the ack now and add contact info.

lina_security: if we confirm dropped entries affecting customer-controlled audit records, legal needs to be looped for notification guidance. Also check contract SLAs for audit retention.

mike_sre: quick update (30m): DLQ scan found ~1200 messages from that window on shard-7; ~980 are parsed and replayable, ~220 failed integrity checks and are quarantined. Starting replay now into the export pipeline to see if ACME's entries show up.

alex_support: Ping — ACME replied: they need a clear timeline and whether we'll provide reconstructed exports or a formal incident report.

lina_security: assume they will want an incident report. If we can reconstruct >95% of entries, propose to offer reconstructed export + root cause + mitigation steps. If reconstruction <95%, coordinate with legal on wording and notification cadence.

mike_sre: replay completed. Preliminary reconciliation: we recovered ~930 of the 980 replayable messages and pushed them to the export consumer. Asking ACME to re-run their export pull — provide a generated temporary export URL once their consumer acknowledges.

alex_support: noted. I'll tell them to try re-export in 30m and give them the temporary S3 URL if needed.

jordan_product: action items summarized:
- SRE: finalize DLQ reconciliation & produce counts (mike)
- Security: draft incident classification & notification triggers (lina)
- Support: customer ack + updates + temporary export URL (alex)
- Product: coordinate customer-facing timeline & contact (jordan)

lina_security: also recommend immediate mitigation: 1) avoid scheduling KMS rotations during controller restarts, 2) add stricter enqueue retry with jitter and longer TTL before dropping to DLQ, 3) update runbook for simultaneous maintenance operations.

mike_sre: filing a postmortem ticket now with preliminary RCA: controller restart + KMS rotation overlap caused transient decrypt errors and a small window of message timeouts leading to DLQ/quarantine. Will include metric graphs and DLQ counts.

alex_support: sent ack to ACME at 2026-03-10T11:05 (their local). Message includes expected initial findings in 3 hours and point of contact (alex_support@redwood.example).

opsbot: incident_ticket_created: INC-2026-0453 by mike_sre

lina_security: thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread; we need a validated timeline and final customer note within 72 hours.

mike_sre: will update with final DLQ reconciliation and exported URL for ACME.

alex_support: ACME confirms they saw the recovered entries after re-export. They want the formal incident report and confirmation of preventive changes.

lina_security: next steps: draft customer-facing incident report (sec + product) and internal postmortem. Target delivery: customer report in 48 hours, internal postmortem in 7 days.

sara: thanks team — keep the thread updated.
